newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria says will participate in Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Austria says will participate in Albania force.

text.p: Austria said on Thursday it was prepared to contribute troops to an international security force in Albania for the protection of relief convoys.
"The cabinet agreed Austrian troops should be sent to Albania, but only to guarantee the passage of aid deliveries," Chancellor Viktor Klima told reporters after a weekly cabinet meeting.
Italy, France, Greece, Turkey, Spain and Romania have already offered to contribute troops to an international stabilisation force in Albania.
Klima said the Austrian contingent would be made up of police and soldiers, but gave no details of its size.
The government would await the exact plan of operation from Italy, which will lead the force, before making any formal decision on sending troops, he added.

Austrian far-right leader Joerg Haider has spoken out against participation in Albania, saying an Italian-led force could be the target of Albanian wrath after the sinking of a ship carrying refugees off the Italian coast.
Albania collapsed into lawlessness after the demise of shady savings schemes sparked mass violent protests.
